info.name: DominoClub — Security Demo (M4 · M5 · M6)
info.description:
Full demonstration of security features across Milestones 4, 5, and 6.

**M4:** Replay protection (nonce), Trust score, GPS impossible movement, GPS accuracy / mock location, Velocity checks (queue & withdrawal), Device binding
**M5:** PIX webhook hardening, Double-spend fix, JWT blacklist, Admin rate limit
**M6 (new):** App Attest Phase 2 (session token), IP-level velocity limit, Real-time bot detection

**HOW TO USE:**
1. Import the Environment file alongside this collection
2. Select 'DominoClub — Local Dev' environment in the top-right corner
3. Run '0 — AUTHENTICATION → Dev Login' first — it saves tokens automatically
4. Execute requests in order within each folder
5. For WebSocket: New → Socket.IO → ws://localhost:3001 → Auth header: Bearer {{access_token}}

item.name: 📍 SCENE 3 — GPS Impossible Movement
item.description:
Demonstrates impossible movement detection.
Send Sao Paulo → wait 15s → send Manaus.
The server calculates ~4000 km in a few seconds = impossible speed.

exec: console.log('📍 Ready. Send GPS from Sao Paulo: -23.5505, -46.6333');
console.log('✅ Token confirmed. Proceed with WebSocket GPS test.');
console.log('⏳ After sending Sao Paulo GPS, wait 15 seconds before sending Manaus!');
console.log('AFTER: Open pgAdmin → FraudLog table → see IMPOSSIBLE_MOVEMENT record.');

Accuracy = 0 is a mock location indicator on Android.
The server accepts it but decrements trust_score and logs the event.

console.log('trust_score:', json.trust_score ?? '(not in this endpoint — check pgAdmin)');
console.log('💡 To see trust_score: pgAdmin → SELECT id, name, trust_score, bot_score FROM "User";');

request.description: Shows the logged-in user's data. The trust_score is visible in pgAdmin after suspicious actions.

item.name: 🛡️ SCENE 5 — Trust Score & Paid Game Block
item.description:
A user with trust_score < 0.45 is blocked from paid games.

MANUAL STEP REQUIRED:
In pgAdmin, set the user's trust_score to 0.30 before running Scene 5b.

exec: console.log('MANUAL STEP: Open pgAdmin and run this SQL:');
console.log('UPDATE "User" SET trust_score = 0.30 WHERE id = \'' + userId + '\';');
console.log('-- After the demo, restore it:');
console.log('UPDATE "User" SET trust_score = 1.0 WHERE id = \'' + userId + '\';');
console.log('  MEDIUM (0.45-0.74): allowed, but flagged in logs');
console.log('  LOW    (< 0.45): BLOCKED from paid games');

request.description:
Run this request to see the SQL in the Postman Console (View → Console).

Then go to pgAdmin and execute the UPDATE to lower the trust_score.

item.name: 5b. ℹ️ INSTRUCTIONS — Try paid game with LOW trust

console.log('Afterwards restore: UPDATE "User" SET trust_score = 1.0 WHERE id = ...');
console.log('  ⚠️ Access allowed, but account is monitored');

request.description:
Shows the current user's security state in real time:

item.name: 💸 SCENE 6 — Velocity Check (Withdrawal)
item.description:
Maximum 3 withdrawals per hour per user.
On the 4th attempt the server returns HTTP 429.

request.description: Withdrawal attempt #1. May return insufficient balance error (normal) — what matters is it does NOT return 429.

This attempt MUST return HTTP 429 with body:
```json
{
  "error": "Withdrawal limit reached. Try again later.",
  "code": "VELOCITY_EXCEEDED"
}
```

The test script confirms this automatically.

item.name: 📱 SCENE 7 — Device Binding
item.description:
Demonstrates that the server records full device history.
Each (userId, device_id) pair is stored in the DeviceBind table.

exec: console.log('💡 Check pgAdmin now: SELECT * FROM "DeviceBind";');
console.log('💡 You should now see 2 records in DeviceBind for the same userId.');

item.name: 7d. Login with Device D — SHOULD TRIGGER ALERT ⚠️

exec: console.log('✅ Logged in with device-D-004 (4th device)');
console.log('   SELECT * FROM "FraudLog" WHERE type = \'DEVICE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED\' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;');
console.log('   Also verify that trust_score was decremented by -0.08');

request.description:
4th device for the same user.

Login is PERMITTED (no hard block yet — flagging phase only),
but generates a DEVICE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED FraudLog and decrements trust_score.

Verify in pgAdmin after running.

item.name: 🔑 SCENE 8 — App Attest Phase 2 (Session Token) [M6]
item.description:
Demonstrates the full App Attest Phase 2 flow.

Phase 1: server issues a session token after successful attestation.
Phase 2: subsequent sessions use the session token instead of re-attesting (Apple rate-limits re-attestation).

The token expires in 48h and is revocable via DeviceBind.is_active.

exec: console.log('✅ Nonce for App Attest Phase 1:', json.nonce);

request.description:
First step of App Attest: the server issues a single-use nonce (UUID, 2-min TTL).
The iOS app uses this nonce as clientData to generate the attestation token.

item.name: 8b. ℹ️ INSTRUCTIONS — Phase 1 via WebSocket (emits session token)

exec: console.log('SCENE 8 — APP ATTEST PHASE 1 + SESSION TOKEN');
integrityNonce: nonce || '(get a nonce in step 8a first)'
console.log('Copy the token and set it as the session_token environment variable.');
console.log('Then run step 8c to demonstrate Phase 2.');

item.name: 8c. ℹ️ INSTRUCTIONS — Phase 2 via WebSocket (uses session token)

exec: const sessionToken = pm.environment.get('session_token') || '(paste token from step 8b here)';
console.log('NO NONCE NEEDED — the session token is self-contained.');
console.log('EXPECTED RESULT: queue:joined (without calling Apple API)');
console.log('pgAdmin: UPDATE "DeviceBind" SET is_active = false WHERE attest_key_id = \'demo-key-id-abc123\';');

request.description:
Returns all fraud-logs. Filter visually by type: INTEGRITY_FAIL to see Phase 1 and Phase 2 failures.

Requires admin_token (run Admin Login in folder 0 — AUTHENTICATION).

item.name: 🌐 SCENE 9 — IP Velocity Limit [M6 New]
item.description:
Demonstrates blocking for too many attempts from the same IP address.
Limit: 20 queue:join per IP in 5 minutes.

Unlike per-user velocity (Scene 2), this block protects against account-farms:
an attacker with 50 accounts behind the same IP is still blocked.

item.name: 9a. ℹ️ INSTRUCTIONS — IP Velocity via WebSocket

exec: console.log('SCENE 9 — IP VELOCITY LIMIT (new in M6)');
console.log('The limit is 20 queue:join per IP in 5 minutes.');
console.log('1. In the WebSocket, emit queue:join 21 times (can use different accounts):');
console.log('On the 21st attempt (from any account on the same IP):');
message: 'Too many attempts from this address. Please wait a few minutes.',
console.log('  Scene 2: blocks the USER after 10 attempts + applies trust signal');
console.log('  Scene 9: blocks the IP after 20 attempts, NO trust penalty');
console.log('           (the IP may be a shared router — penalising trust would be unfair)');

item.name: 🤖 SCENE 10 — Real-Time Bot Detection [M6 New]
item.description:
Demonstrates bot detection DURING a match (not just at the end).

Before (M4): bot_score was only calculated when the match finished — the bot may have already won the prize.
Now (M6): after 10 moves with 60%+ under 800ms, the server emits game:bot_suspicion to the suspected player.

item.name: 10a. ℹ️ INSTRUCTIONS — Observe bot_suspicion via WebSocket

exec: console.log('1. Start a match normally (queue:join + game:join)');
console.log('2. Emit game:move or game:draw rapidly 10+ times');
console.log('3. The server will emit to your private user:{id} room:');
console.log('4. In the server terminal, look for:');
console.log('NOTE: the signal does not immediately block — it is an');
console.log('alert. trust_score is adjusted at match end by updateBotScore');

request.description:
Returns BOT_PATTERN fraud-logs — generated at the end of each suspicious match.

Each record shows:
- fastRatio: % of moves below 800ms
- avgMoveMs: average time per move
- botScore: user's accumulated EMA score (0–1)

Requires admin_token.

exec: console.log('  ⚠️ Access allowed, account is monitored');
console.log('  ✅ Account is in good standing');

request.description:
Shows the current user's security state in real time:
- trust_score (0–1)
- trust_level (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW)
- bot_score (0–1, calculated post-match)
- can_join_paid (false when trust < 0.45)

Great for showing the live effect of fraud signals on a user's profile.
